items.note: No initial detector cool-down time is stated for the MOBIUS-ST / GEM Streamline CFG-SV. The Mobius brochure (snapshot 3c63f2bd59172808) gives only LN2 holding time (7-10 days for a Streamline cryostat) and the 2-year no-refill claim; the GEM configuration guide (8f581ef570485c0a) mentions only a 'typical three day loss of use' after a warm-up of a standard cryostat, which is not a cooldown spec. Web searches found no ORTEC figure; generic HPGe cooldown advice (2-8 h) is not model-specific and was not used.

items.quote: Cool Down Time to 100 Kelvin 20 minutes
items.document_title: 800 Series Cryostream Cooler (user manual, Oxford Cryosystems Ltd, 2014)
items.note: Manufacturer technical data: cool down time to 100 K (the controller's default start-up command is 'Cool to 100.0 K'). The configuration base is 80 K; no separate time to 80 K is stated, so this is the documented cooldown to the standard operating temperature.

items.quote: Note that the time needed to cool down the insert from room temperature and 0.3 K is about 2.5 hours.
items.document_title: HelioxVT quick reference for the Dolly instrument (Paul Scherrer Institut, June 2017)
items.note: Facility (PSI Dolly muSR instrument) user guide for its Oxford Instruments HelioxVT, not a manufacturer spec and not a peer-reviewed paper; that installation runs in a Variox VTI with a Mercury controller rather than the ITC503 of HELVT30SYS. The 2003 manufacturer product guide (doc_oxford_instruments_helioxvt_0, snapshot d6171861a022a5d4) only says the condensation and the cool down time typically require less than 1 hour, counted after the VTI has precooled the insert from 300 K to ~10 K, so it is not a room-temperature-to-base time.

No cooldown time of the LN2-cooled wide-temperature-range electrode to -150 C is published. The ICP-RIE product page (fff4988644a3856d) and the PlasmaPro 100 brochure (plasma.oxinst.com/assets/uploads/PlasmaPro_100_6.pdf, 6246453e02570da5) give no time; the only timing found is for the separate LN2 Auto Changeover upgrade (200 C to 20 C in 40 min), which is not a cooldown to the cryo set point, so it was not used.

No pull-down time for the MDF-DC500VX chest freezer was found: the PHCbi global and EU product pages (c8de52373b7aab3f, 83268f0154c1a2d7) list only cooling performance (-86 C), and no DC500VX data sheet with a pull-down figure or curve could be retrieved (vitaris leaflet 404, directindustry catalogue 403). Upright TwinGuard data sheets are other models and were not used.

items.quote: Pull-Down Time from 20ºC Ambient Setpoint -70ºC | Setpoint -80ºC 4.5 hours | 5.5 hours
items.document_title: MDF-DU702VH-PA Technical Data Sheet (PHCbi, ENERGY STAR certified upright ULT freezer; copy hosted by distributor BSI)
items.note: PHC technical data sheet for MDF-DU702VH-PA, the 220 V North-American variant of the same VIP ECO model (same 729 L volume and 870 x 600 x 1400 mm interior as the global data sheet). Pull-down from 20 C ambient to the -80 C setpoint is 5.5 h (4.5 h to -70 C). The global data sheet in the equipment file shows only a pull-down curve without a printed number. No time to -86 C is given.

No pull-down time for the MDF-MU339HL(-PE) was found: the PHC Europe product page (d204c7435235c116) lists only cooling performance (-30 C); no technical data sheet with a pull-down figure could be located (the ENERGY STAR listing renders via JavaScript; the inycom catalogue was unreachable and covers MDF-MU339, not HL).

items.quote: The cooldown time from room temperature to the base temperature is around 30 hours.
items.document_title: Cryogen-free dilution refrigerator - Proteox MX450 (CISUP, University of Pisa instrument page)
items.note: University facility statement for its installed Proteox MX450 (ProteoxMX, 360 mm plate, exchangeable second insert, wiring listed, no magnet mentioned); not a manufacturer specification and not a peer-reviewed paper. QD Oxford's ProteoxMX page and brochure give only sample-puck cooldowns (<8 h with the bottom loader), which do not apply to this no-loader configuration, and no full-system cooldown time.

items.quote: Cool down from ambient to 77.2 K 20 mins
items.document_title: Optistats - Automated & Compact Optical Cryostats for Spectroscopy (Quantum Design Oxford specification matrix, OPTSS 0926 R5)
items.note: One value shared by the OptistatDN and OptistatDN-V columns. The product page agrees: 'System Cooldown: ~ 20 Minutes to 77 K' in the OptistatDN-V section.

items.document_title: Optical cryostats for spectroscopy - Optistat (Quantum Design Oxford product page)
items.note: OptistatCF-V (sample in vacuum) helium-flow cooldown to 4.2 K. The specification matrix (OPTSS 0926 R5, page 5, snapshot c73e273061693731) gives 'Cool down from ambient to 4.2 K' 25 min (OptistatCF) and 10 min (CF-V). Excludes the time to set up the external LHe storage dewar and transfer line.

Qualitest's specification (c933174d0b24c576) gives only staged cooling speeds at 25 C ambient (room temperature to 0 C: 2 C/min; 0 to -40 C: 1.5 C/min; -40 to -80 C: 1.3 C/min; -80 to -100 C: 0.8 C/min), not a pull-down time to a set point. A time could only be computed from these rates, which would be a derived estimate, so it is not reported.

The Qualitest QualiBrittle NDA specification table (8ba46dff0556ce34) lists temperature range, accuracy and striker data only; no cooling/pull-down time to -70 C (compressor) or -120 C (LN2 option) is published. The 5 min figure is the specimen soak time, not a cooldown.
